facts.title: What Renegade is
facts.answer: Renegade is a Windows-first game engine and creator environment built on Wicked Engine. Renegade Studio is the editor; your own game project is separate. This assistant does not control the editor unless an explicit, verified bridge is connected.

sources.needle: Renegade is a Windows-first game engine and creator environment

facts.title: Surface Type and glass impact routing
facts.answer: For a selected scene object, the documented creator workflow is to choose Surface Type in its Inspector. The source-defined types include Default, Metal, Wood, Concrete, Stone, Dirt / Ground, Glass, Water and Character. Glass uses the 'Glass' classification. I have not inspected your selected object or confirmed an effect is playing; first verify the object's Surface Type and then test the impact.

sources.needle: Creator steps: select an object; choose Surface Type directly in its Inspector.

facts.title: Current selection and assistant access
facts.answer: Renegade has a SelectionService with HasSelection() and SelectedEntity(). This is an engine facility, not proof that the assistant can see what you selected: a read-only Editor Context Broker must be connected before the assistant may claim to inspect an object.

facts.title: Undo and safe assistant edits
facts.answer: Renegade's existing CommandService exposes Execute, Undo and Redo. That is the intended authority for future approved assistant edits, but a command's existence does not mean the assistant can execute it. No change may be reported as applied without a verified editor execution receipt.

facts.title: Projectile Spawn Point firing choices
facts.answer: The native Player Projectile Editor defines Spawn point and Firing controls. Its firing policies include Selected spawn point. This is evidence of editor control definitions, not evidence that your current weapon is configured correctly. The assistant cannot inspect that weapon until a read-only Studio bridge is connected.

facts.title: Physical projectiles and instant hitscan
facts.answer: In Weapon firing, Fire mode has two native choices: Projectile / travelling and Hitscan / instant ray. The former fires an authored travelling projectile asset; the latter uses a ray, range and damage controls without selecting a travelling projectile. This describes editor controls, not your current weapon configuration.

facts.title: NEW projectile versus EDIT COPY
facts.answer: In Weapon firing, NEW starts a fresh Bullet-based projectile draft. EDIT COPY loads the currently selected projectile into a separate copy draft, leaving the source asset unchanged. Both must be saved with SAVE AS NEW to create a reusable projectile; saving a projectile alone does not assign it to the player's weapon.

facts.title: Arrow preset starting speed and gravity
facts.answer: The Arrow preset starts at speed 45 metres per second and gravity scale 1; these values are editable starting points, not enforced defaults for all arrows. Select a visible model if you need an actual arrow mesh. A NEW weapon projectile draft initially selects Bullet until you choose Arrow.

facts.title: Single or multiple weapon launch points
facts.answer: A newly authored weapon binding with one launch point automatically selects that point. The Firing policy dropdown is normally hidden when only one point is available; when there are multiple authored points it exposes Selected spawn point, Alternate between two and Both together. If a saved multi-point policy needs repair, the dropdown may remain visible.

facts.title: Weapon animation fire/release timing
facts.answer: Weapon firing provides Fire at: Animation start or After a delay. SET FIRE TIME IN ANIMATION opens the selected weapon action's preview when available. MARK CURRENT POSE captures a candidate timing and USE FIRE TIME transfers it; the marker must be nonnegative, before clip end and at most five seconds. If preview data are unavailable, use the numeric delay. Applying to the player is still a separate step.

sources.needle: This action has no animation to preview. Use the numeric delay.

facts.title: Save projectile versus apply weapon binding to player
facts.answer: SAVE AS NEW creates a reusable projectile asset. To equip it, return to Weapon firing, select the projectile and relevant action, then use APPLY TO THIS PLAYER. Renegade saves a new equipment definition and uses the command service to update this Player Start's equipment assignment. Save the level to retain the assignment. No assistant edit has been executed.

facts.title: Sticking projectile needs a visible model
facts.answer: A projectile configured to Stick into the object must reference a valid visible imported model; Renegade's asset validation rejects stick-on-impact when meshAssetId is empty. Set the Visible model first, then select Stick into the object; available lifetime and embed-depth controls are in Advanced.

facts.title: Renegade rivers: spline flow, foam, width and tributaries
facts.answer: Renegade Studio has editable spline rivers. The River V2 controls include ENABLE SPLINE FLOW + FOAM, flow arrows, river speed, contact foam, node-by-node width, and tributary connections. Select a river or control node to inspect the available settings. These source-verified controls do not prove that the released river is fitting the terrain correctly: alignment is under investigation in pre-alpha 2026.11.01.1.

facts.title: River width, bed and terrain banks
facts.answer: River-node width is set in metres under SELECTED NODE WIDTH. If Riverbed & Banks displays CHANNEL // NOT LINKED, the LINK / UPDATE BED button is the intended channel-cut action; moving spline points then updates the linked channel, and REMOVE BED restores the base terrain. Use a COPIED project when investigating existing gaps, and use Undo if needed. If water floats, crosses banks or does not fit after linking, that is a reported pre-alpha defect, not expected behaviour. Preserve the project and a screenshot.

sources.needle: Width in metres at this point; the nearby channel and linked banks follow smoothly.
Linked riverbeds update with the river.

facts.title: Renegade waterfall placement and spray controls
facts.answer: Waterfalls have their own placement controls. ADD WATERFALL creates a waterfall without requiring a river; use CREST / TOP and LANDING / BOTTOM to move its handles. Available visual controls include width, flow/intensity, turbulence, airborne spray, ambient mist and impact spray. This describes the present UI; it does not claim the current pre-alpha has passed every visual or terrain-alignment test.

facts.title: How to draw a river and link it to the terrain in Renegade Studio
facts.answer: To draw a river: 1. Open the Terrain river controls and select DRAW RIVER. 2. Left-drag across the terrain to draw its water spline; release to finish. 3. Select the new River Water in the scene or hierarchy. 4. In RIVERBED & BANKS adjust BED DEPTH and BANK WIDTH, then press LINK / UPDATE BED. 5. Check that its channel reports linked and that the water meets the banks. On brand-new flat terrain, ALLOW DEEPER BEDS +10M may first be needed if the desired bed extends below the terrain height range. If the water does not fit after linking, that is a reported 2026.11.01.1 defect; do not assume it is fixed. These are source-checked controls; full fresh-extract Studio workflow acceptance is pending.

sources.needle: Then select the new River Water and click LINK / UPDATE BED to cut the channel.
